beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: You think Mark Zuckerberg lives on his paycheck?

params.header: So how is he this rich?

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: So how is he this rich?

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: Because his money was never a paycheck.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: He owns shares of Meta, and when the company grows, his shares grow with it.

actions.text: Where does the cash come from?

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: But you can't buy a house with shares. Where does the cash come from?

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: Selling shares would mean paying tax on the gain.

actions.name: Collateral
actions.line: What the bank keeps if you don't pay

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: So the very rich often borrow against their shares instead.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Hold on. So they never pay any tax at all?

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: They pay a little. Take the twenty-five richest Americans.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: In five years, their wealth grew $401B. Their federal income tax: $13.6B.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: Divide the tax by the growth: their true tax rate was just 3.4%.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Just 3.4%? My tax comes out before my paycheck even reaches me!

actions.name: Unrealized gain
actions.line: Growth you haven't sold isn't taxed

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: A paycheck is taxed the day it's paid, but shares that grow aren't taxed until they're sold.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: So the one-dollar salary was never the point. Would you rather own a paycheck, or the company?
